prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1236; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of the roadway in League City, Texas, when the vehicle attempted a lane change to the right. Driver 2, operating a vehicle in the adjacent lane, was unable to avoid contact, and the two vehicles sideswiped one another along their passenger-side and driver-side panels. Driver 1 stated that the impact caused neck and back pain, and the reported symptoms are consistent with the forces typical of a collision of this kind. Damage visible on both vehicles lines up with the described point of contact, and photographs taken at the scene confirm several of the details provided by the drivers. No independent witnesses were located, and no one else observed the collision itself. Officers confirmed through statements from the drivers and from the Passenger, who was seated in the rear of Driver 1's vehicle, that the Passenger was present at the time of impact. Responding officers found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle involved. Records checked at the scene show that Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering that vehicle.
